D020-D013_h025.question:
I’ve been feeling off since my last shift—about three months now. After the warehouse fire where we lost a civilian, I just haven’t been the same. I can’t shake this heaviness. I barely sleep, and when I do, I wake up exhausted. I used to look forward to coming home to my wife, but now I don’t have the energy to talk, or even to shower most days. I’ve lost interest in everything—hunting, working out, even the team barbecues. I feel worthless, like I failed that night, and I keep thinking I don’t deserve to be happy. Food tastes like nothing, and I’ve lost about 10 pounds without trying. Some days, I wonder if my wife would be better off without me. 

I know I’ve been drinking more—off-duty, nothing that breaks fireground rules—but I’ve also started speeding on my way home, not caring about traffic, and I got a ticket last month, which is unlike me. My captain noticed I’ve been short with the crew. It’s not just reacting to the stress—I feel broken. The sadness isn’t fading, and it’s affecting every part of my life.
